evidence: src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: FulfilmentService exposes addProduct, listProducts, placeOrder, advanceOrder, cancelOrder, listOrders and getOrder, all fulfilment use cases built on ProductRepository and OrderRepository.
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: the private helpers requireProduct and requireOrder hold the not-found rule (NotFoundError) in one place, and every method that looks up an entity uses them.
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: toProductView and toOrderView are the only mappers to the exported ProductView and OrderView types.

src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: placeOrder checks `product.availableStock < quantity` before `product.reserve(quantity)`, and a comment says this keeps an unsuccessful request atomic, so it is coordination across order lines rather than a stray duplicate.
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts: combineItems is the single place that validates and merges PlaceOrderItem input into OrderLine[].
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is one file, src/application/fulfilment-service.ts, and it covers a single concern: application-level use cases for fulfilment. FulfilmentService manages the product catalogue and the order lifecycle through the injected ProductRepository and OrderRepository. It maps entities to view types (OrderView, ProductView) through one pair of private mappers. The service uses its own helpers consistently. requireProduct and requireOrder hold the not-found rule in one place, toProductView and toOrderView are the only mapping paths, and combineItems is the only place that normalises order input. Every public method goes through these helpers and none of them bypasses them. Two checks may repeat rules held elsewhere. First, placeOrder compares product.availableStock with quantity before calling product.reserve. Second, combineItems checks that quantities are positive integers, which the Order constructor may also check. The domain source wasn't provided, so I can't confirm either case. The stock pre-check is also documented as deliberate, to keep a failed multi-line order atomic, which is a coordination concern that belongs in the application layer. Neither case is clear enough to count as a violation.
